questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles file and network handles? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Importer.Sync calls defer tx.Rollback() right after BeginTx, even though the happy path ends in tx.Commit(). Why is that safe and useful?
choices: Rollback after Commit undoes the commit, so the deferred call must be conditional.
It rolls back every transaction on exit, so Commit has no effect.
It only runs if the context is cancelled.
After a successful Commit, Rollback returns sql.ErrTxDone and does nothing; on any early return it releases the connection and discards partial work.

questions.prompt: ActiveItems checks rows.Err() after the loop even though every Scan error is handled. Why?
choices: rows.Next() returns false both at the end of the data and when iteration fails, so Err distinguishes a truncated result from a complete one.
Scan errors are only reported by rows.Err().
It is required to release the connection back to the pool.

questions.prompt: In Fetch, when io.Copy fails the code calls tmp.Close() and os.Remove(tmp.Name()) before returning. Why is that needed?
choices: Because os.CreateTemp files are deleted automatically only if closed.
Because the caller only removes the path Fetch returns on success; on error no one else knows the file name, so it would stay on disk with an open descriptor.
To flush buffered data so the HTTP client can reuse the connection.
Because io.Copy leaves the file locked.
